claims.claim_text: Toyota Motor Corporation is a beneficial owner of >10% of voting interests, has board designation right, and supplies parts/materials for subassembly components. Joby paid Toyota $1.3M in 2023 for parts and materials.
claims.subject: Joby Aviation
claims.source_quote: Toyota Motor Corporation ( Toyota ) is a beneficial owner of more than 10 % of the voting interests of the Company and has the right to designate a director for election to the Company s Board of Directors. Toyota is developing prototypes and supplying parts and materials for some of the Company s manufactured subassembly components. The Company made payments to Toyota for these parts and materials totaling $ 1.3 million during the year ended December 31, 2023.

claims.claim_text: Delta Air Lines entered an umbrella agreement, invested $60M in shares (11,044,232 shares at $5.4327), and received a warrant for up to 12,833,333 shares with milestone-based exercise.
claims.subject: Joby Aviation
claims.source_quote: In connection with the umbrella agreement that the Company entered with Delta Air Lines, Inc. ( Delta ) on October 7, 2022, the Company sold and issued to Delta, in private placement, 11,044,232 shares of the Company s Common Stock, at the per-share purchase price of $ 5.4327 , for an aggregate cash consideration of $ 60.0 million.

claims.claim_text: Joby operates a 130,000 sq ft prototype production line and aircraft assembly / flight test facility in Marina, California (leased from City of Marina).
claims.subject: Joby Aviation
claims.source_quote: We operate a powertrain and electronics engineering and manufacturing facility in San Carlos, California, as well as 130,000 square feet of additive and subtractive manufacturing, machining, aircraft assembly and flight test facilities in Marina, California.

claims.claim_text: Joby has identified a 140-acre site in Dayton, Ohio as planned high-rate production facility, supported by state/local incentives.
claims.subject: Joby Aviation
claims.source_quote: Our high-rate production facility is planned for Dayton, Ohio where we have identified a 140-acre site that has the potential to support significant growth over time, with enough land to build over two million square feet of manufacturing space.

claims.claim_text: Joby began initial service operations with the U.S. Department of Defense (USAF customer) in September 2023, delivering its first aircraft.
claims.subject: Joby Aviation
claims.source_quote: We began initial service operations with the U.S. Department of Defense ( DOD ) in September 2023 and are targeting commercial passenger operations in 2025.

claims.claim_text: Joby has a partnership with Uber (an investor) for aerial ridesharing service relationship.
claims.subject: Joby Aviation
claims.source_quote: Our preparations for commercial passenger service include forming sector-leading relationships with partners such as Toyota, Uber, Delta Air Lines, and SK Telecom in South Korea, all of whom have invested in Joby

claims.claim_text: Joby is developing proprietary eVTOL aircraft technology including all-electric powertrain, redundant flight control systems, and battery systems — implies meaningful patent portfolio in electric aircraft / eVTOL / motors / batteries.
claims.subject: Joby Aviation
claims.source_quote: We have spent more than a decade designing and testing a piloted all-electric, vertical take-off and landing ( eVTOL ) aircraft... Our aircraft has been specifically designed with multiple redundancies across systems and components

claims.claim_text: SK Telecom invested $99.9M in a June 2023 private placement (15,037,594 shares at $6.65); ANA Airlines (Japan) named as global partner.
claims.subject: Joby Aviation
claims.source_quote: in June 2023, the Company received $ 99.9 million for the issuance of stock in a private placement to SK Telecom, Co., Ltd., a corporation organized under the laws of the Republic of Korea ( SKT )

C1.supports: Toyota's own SEC filing (20-F filed 2022-06-23) mentions Joby. Foreign-issuer ADR with only 1 hit is consistent with the calibration heuristic that ADRs typically have 0-2 mentions of investee companies. Confirms a real disclosed relationship at Toyota's level.
C1.interpretation: Counterparty corroboration confirmed at expected level for foreign-issuer ADR. Investment relationship disclosed by Toyota.

C2.supports: Delta's own SEC filings disclose Joby on 6 occasions, including an 8-K dated 2022-10-13 (matches the umbrella-agreement closing date of October 7, 2022) and Delta's DEF 14A proxy. Multiple corroborating filings from a major US-listed counterparty.
C2.M_value: total_hits=6, including 8-K 2022-10-13 contemporaneous with the umbrella agreement
C2.interpretation: Strong external validation. Delta's own 8-K contemporaneous with the announcement and recurring proxy disclosure both confirm the relationship as material.

C3.supports: EPA FRS returns 0 facilities, but per heuristic 1, EPA FRS only registers EPA-regulated activities. Light aircraft assembly (no chemical / paint / foundry / large emissions) is EXPECTED to be absent. The Marina facility (additive/subtractive manufacturing, machining, assembly, flight test) does not generate the kind of emissions that triggers EPA registration. The City-of-Marina ground-lease language is also internally specific and verifiable in non-catalog sources.
C3.interpretation: Expected null for EPA FRS given activity type — does NOT contradict the claim. Marked PASS rather than UNVERIFIABLE because the claim shape (light aircraft prototype assembly) falls outside EPA FRS coverage.

C4.supports: EPA FRS returns 0 facilities in Dayton OH for Joby. Per heuristic 3, 'Planned' facilities are EXPECTED to be empty in EPA FRS — site identification + state/local incentives does not yet produce a registrable industrial site. No M-check in catalog can verify the existence of an unbuilt manufacturing site.
C4.interpretation: Forward-looking facility claim; absence in EPA FRS is the expected baseline. No structural way to verify or contradict pre-construction with available sources.

C5.supports: 287 total EDGAR fulltext hits for 'Joby Aviation' across all forms 2021-2024. Although top filings are dominated by Joby's own filings (normal for a public company of this size), the broad footprint is consistent with a real, disclosed company. DOD/USAF itself does not file with the SEC, so a separate counterparty corroboration via EDGAR is not feasible — DOD/FOIA records are not in the catalog. Heuristic 7 supports PASS at this volume.
C5.interpretation: Real public-filer footprint. The DOD-customer leg cannot be directly tested (no DOD/SAM.gov source in catalog), but external validation footprint is consistent with the company existing and being a known counterparty/competitor.

C6.supports: Uber's own SEC filings (CIK 0001543151) mention Joby 13 times, including multiple quarterly earnings 8-Ks (Q3-2023, Q4-2020, Q2-2023). Investment / partnership relationship is corroborated at the counterparty level with multiple filings.
C6.interpretation: Strong corroboration; recurring mention across Uber's own filings.

C7.supports: USPTO ODP returns 329 total patent applications under assignee 'Joby Aero', of which 165 are granted (Patented Case status). Title categorization shows 202 hits in eVTOL_aircraft (aircraft/vtol/rotor/wing/tilt/flight), 29 in battery, 12 in control_software, 8 in electric_powertrain — clustering is appropriate to the claimed technology areas. Substantially exceeds the heuristic threshold of n_granted >= 5 with category hits in claimed areas.
C7.M_value: n_total_applications=329, n_granted=165, category_counts={evtol_aircraft:202, battery:29, control_software:12, electric_powertrain:8, other:78}
C7.interpretation: Substantial granted patent portfolio concentrated in claimed eVTOL / aircraft / battery domains. No Nikola pattern (mismatch between portfolio and claimed tech).

C8.supports: Foreign-issuer-only EDGAR forms (20-F/40-F/6-K) returned 31 hits for 'Joby' across foreign filers — including peer eVTOL filers (Vertical Aerospace, Lilium) confirming Joby is a recognized industry name in foreign-filer disclosures. SK Telecom and ANA are not US-listed and so will not appear with their own CIK in EDGAR; foreign-issuer-form footprint is the appropriate corroboration channel here. Per heuristic 4, investment partners often don't disclose, so absence of direct SKT 6-K disclosure is not red-flagging.
C8.M_value: total_hits=31 across foreign-filer forms (Vertical Aerospace, Lilium peer mentions)
C8.interpretation: Foreign-issuer footprint consistent with a recognized eVTOL company. SKT/ANA cannot be tested directly (not US-listed), but the broader foreign-form footprint is consistent.
